title: Capacitor dielectric, ESR and ripple qualification

provenance.citation: IEC 60384 fixed capacitor terminology and manufacturer application notes
provenance.locator: dielectric classes, ESR and ripple current
provenance.note: Starter pack contains model structure and test methods only; every part value must come from a revision-bound datasheet or measurement.

terminology.definition: The ceramic formulation (for example C0G, X7R, X5R, Y5V) that fixes capacitance change over temperature, voltage and time.

provenance.citation: IEC 60384 fixed capacitors for use in electronic equipment
provenance.note: Class II dielectrics are not interchangeable even at the same nominal capacitance and voltage.

terminology.definition: The resistive part of the capacitor impedance at a stated frequency and temperature; it drives self-heating and ripple voltage.

provenance.note: ESR is conditional on frequency and temperature; a 100 kHz value is not a DC value.

terminology.definition: The RMS current the capacitor may carry at a stated frequency and case temperature while staying inside its life and temperature limits.

provenance.note: Ripple ratings require frequency correction and often a case-temperature derating.

provenance.citation: Capacitor manufacturer application notes and IEC 60384-1 endurance practice
provenance.note: The model is an engineering limit model, not a lifetime prediction without a life-test basis.

variables.description: equivalent series resistance at the stated frequency
thermal resistance of the mounted part

equations.expression: C_actual within C_nominal +/- tolerance over the applicability envelope

variables.description: capacitance at the stated bias, frequency and temperature

provenance.note: Class II capacitance is bias and temperature dependent; tolerance is not a constant.

assumptions.statement: The ripple current is sinusoidal and its RMS value is known at the relevant frequency.

provenance.note: A non-sinusoidal ripple requires harmonic weighting.

assumptions.statement: The mounted thermal resistance is known or conservatively bounded by the test article.

provenance.note: A missing thermal path makes the temperature rise unavailable.

validity_domains.statement: ESR and ripple values apply at the stated measurement frequency; extrapolation outside it is invalid.
exclusions: DC bias above the datasheet test condition without a bias curve

validity_domains.statement: The thermal-rise model applies only inside the measured case-temperature range.
exclusions: operation above the rated category temperature

property_sources.property: capacitance, voltage rating, ESR, ripple current, case size

provenance.note: A headline capacitance without test conditions is not a fact.

design_rules.rule: Do not substitute a Class II dielectric without checking capacitance change over temperature, DC bias and aging.
design_rules.check: dielectric class and bias/temperature curves are revision-bound

design_rules.rule: Compare ESR and ripple current at the same frequency and temperature; a missing condition is unavailable, not a pass.
design_rules.check: ESR and ripple limits share the measurement conditions

design_rules.rule: Apply the manufacturer's voltage and temperature derating; nominal voltage alone is not a qualification.
design_rules.check: derating curve and category temperature are recorded

manufacturing_rules.rule: Use the component's specified reflow profile and MSL handling; exceeding it changes ESR and leakage.

failure_modes.cause: electrolyte loss or dielectric degradation under sustained ripple heating
failure_modes.detection: periodic ESR measurement, ripple life test, case temperature rise

failure_modes.cause: Class II dielectric polarization and aging
failure_modes.detection: bias-dependent capacitance measurement at the operating voltage

failure_modes.cause: board flexure, thermal shock or handling
failure_modes.detection: visual inspection, acoustic microscopy, flex test

diagnostic_signatures.signature: ESR above the datasheet limit at the operating frequency and temperature
diagnostic_signatures.indicates: wrong dielectric/part, aging, or a measurement at a different condition

diagnostic_signatures.signature: case temperature rise above the predicted ripple heating
diagnostic_signatures.indicates: insufficient ripple rating, poor mounting, or missing thermal path

test_methods.method: Four-terminal impedance/ESR measurement at the specified frequency and temperature
Ripple current life test at rated case temperature with periodic ESR and capacitance measurement
test_methods.measures: ripple current capability, ESR drift, capacitance drift

test_methods.method: Verify dielectric class and capacitance over temperature, DC bias and aging
Dimensional inspection of case length, width and height against the footprint
Board flex and thermal-shock test with crack inspection

worked_cases.description: A 1 A RMS ripple through 50 mohm ESR dissipates 50 mW; with a 20 K/W mounted path the case rises 1 K above ambient.

provenance.note: Structure only; no part-specific lifetime is inferred.

counterexamples.claim: Any 10 uF 25 V capacitor is interchangeable.
counterexamples.refutation: A Y5V part with the same nominal capacitance loses most of it under DC bias and has a much higher ESR and lower ripple rating.

known_traps.trap: Matching nominal capacitance and voltage while ignoring dielectric class, ESR and ripple rating.
known_traps.why_shallow_fails: The alternate looks electrically identical at the catalogue headline but fails bias, ripple heating and tolerance requirements.
known_traps.guard: Require dielectric class, ESR at the operating frequency, ripple current at case temperature and case dimensions as separate mandatory facts.

known_traps.trap: Comparing an ESR measured at a different frequency or temperature.
known_traps.why_shallow_fails: ESR is strongly frequency- and temperature-dependent; the comparison is dimensionally valid but conditionally invalid.
known_traps.guard: Bind the ESR requirement and the candidate fact to the same measurement condition and derive an impedance test when the condition is missing.
